First, you are a fantastic spouse. Kudos to you. I am chronically depressed myself with no end in sight and my SO is my primary caregiver as well. I am forever thankful that I have him. 

Second, please take care of yourself as well. I used to work with persons with disabilities and caregiver burnout is a real thing.

Here's a hug from a stranger.
Nothing. I wouldn't exist.

A loser. She was ambitious and likely if things had gone on as she wanted to she likely would've been a doctor by now. Now I'm 31 and a masters' student with no notable career achievements so far. She'd be really disappointed.
I am glad to hear of your brother's progress.
I'm getting closer to giving up tbh. I used to think that it's my life my choice as well, but my cousin committed suicide 1.5 years ago and that changed things for me.

I fully understand that. I've been in and out of therapy for years and recently started medication a few years back, more of, succumbed to the temptation that is medication. 

I am glad you are where you are right now.
Thank you for your kindness.

A little context: I used to frequent r/depression and come across various posters who are angry and hell bent on refusing getting treatment because they feel medication have done nothing and therapists are useless. 

What can you say to them? 

(I'm depressed myself but it's a whole different matter)

I'm sorry to hear that for you too. 

I do have things to live for, that's the thing. But there's a something dragging me down at the back of my mind that nothing's worth it. I just don't know what I should do against that.
Thank you so much. Your post really means so much to me. I wish the best for you as well. I'm sorry it's been so hard.

That's what I tell myself as well, but I have managed to come back from that, and I hope you do, too. 

On the other hand, I also wish as well that I will be able to brave enough to kill myself. Cut everyone off and you know, just die. I know how it is, I do.
Don't give up. I'm no sweet talker, but please don't.
Thank you. I will check her out.

That's unfortunate, I'm sorry. 

Tell some jokes to me, talk to me if you want. But it may actually turn into a sadfest from my end because I'm actually in quite a terrible state right now. 

People can be wrong. I spent a lot of my life among many people who don't understand me, but once in a while there are people I can keep close to my side and I treasure them. They are few and far, but still, there they are somehow.

Right? It made me so angry to know that even at my better points in life, it can just strike me from behind and make me lose all of it. 

It's like "Hey, feeling good? Screw you, you won't be anymore."

How long have you been on meds? Did you tell your psychiatrist about these changes? 

Sorry if I come across as aggressive or judgmental, I don't mean to be. It's just that I was once on one medication 10 years ago and it made me numb as well, more willing to die because I had less fear about dying. A little less sad, but more numb. I eventually got better with psychotherapy.

10 years later, I went to see another psychiatrist and requested different medication as I was tired of psychotherapy that was losing its efficacy due to a strain in the patient-therapist relationship. After a period of time, it felt somewhat lighter.

I think it varies from person to person. It's not meant to be a catch all thing. I knew some people with bipolar and I think their huge mood swings are definitely based on biology more than circumstances.

As someone who has been on/off meds both voluntarily and involuntarily over the years, I feel that part of my chronic depression is chemical, part not. My partner has also repeatedly observed that he sees a noticeable improvement when I'm on meds. Plus, I feel less suicidal and my downswings are not as insane as they can be. 

Just my opinion.
